intro.title: How many cash advances may run at once
intro.body: So that people finish off their older cash advances before asking for a new one. There are two numbers for you to set: how many may run at the same time, and how long one may wait to be realized.
intro.rulesTitle: Four things people often get wrong — none of them is visible from the numbers in the table:
intro.ruleBranch: The quota belongs to a branch, not to a person. Someone working across two branches has two separate quotas. Running out at one branch does not close the door at the other.
intro.ruleRelease: A cash advance only stops using its quota once the realization paperwork reaches Finance. Approval from a manager is not enough on its own. And if Finance undoes the receipt, it goes back to using the quota.
intro.ruleDays: The clock starts the day the money is paid out — not the day the cash advance was submitted or approved. Weekends count too.
intro.ruleScope: Only cash advances whose money has already gone out are counted. One still waiting for a manager's signature uses no quota, because there is nothing the requester can do about paperwork sitting on someone else's desk.
intro.liveNotice: This number is checked the moment a requester hits Submit; it is not stored on the document. So if you lower it, the new rule applies to everyone straight away — including people who happen to be holding more cash advances than the new limit. They cannot submit again until their count comes down.

list.title: Cash Advance Limit Master
list.subtitle: When several limits cover the same person, the most specific one is used: a department limit beats an area limit, and both beat the general limit.

form.name: Limit Name
form.branchesHint: Pick one or several branches. Left empty, it applies to every branch.
form.departmentsHint: Pick one or several departments. Left empty, it applies to every department.
form.maxOutstandingHint: How many cash advances one person may have running at the same time, at one branch.
form.maxDaysHint: Counted from the day the money is paid out. Weekends count too.
form.notesPlaceholder: Optional. For example, why this limit differs.
form.isUnlimitedHint: This limit does not limit anything: the number of running FPUs and the age of their realisations are ignored. Used e.g. for the BOD. Both numbers above are kept and apply again as soon as this is switched off.
